NSH.head: The Predators face a real test
NSH.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators can pull it off if they get good looks.

CAR.head: Advantage, the Hurricanes
CAR.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators’ way back in is getting good looks.

story.head: The Predators give up shots, and the Hurricanes take them
paras: The Predators (4-4-5) lost 4-3 to Washington on Thursday, while the Hurricanes have won three straight. Going in, the Canes are first in the NHL and the Predators sixth in the Central (tied for 22nd in the NHL).

The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). Carolina has scored 3.73 goals a game, the third most in the league, and allowed 2.33, the third fewest. The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest), get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (30th). The Hurricanes are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Predators. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Sebastian Aho (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 15 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with six goals in six games against Nashville since 2023-24. Logan Stankoven (9 G / 3 A / 12 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL. Steven Stamkos (7 G / 8 A / 15 P in 13 GP) is tied for the Predators’ scoring lead. Filip Forsberg (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 13 GP) shares it, with seven points in his last five games.
Pyotr Kochetkov (9-0-0 / .918 SV% in 9 GS) has been outstanding for Carolina and will likely start. Juuse Saros (3-3-4 / .902 SV% in 10 GS) is in line to start for Nashville.
The Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Predators do.

items.text: Pyotr Kochetkov has won all nine of his starts this season, already the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history.
The Hurricanes have been without Taylor Hall, Jordan Staal and Alexander Nikishin for several games.
Mark Jankowski has six goals on chances worth about 2.6 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Jackson Blake and Nikolaj Ehlers have a point in five straight games.
